title: Detained immigrants launch hunger strike against prolonged detention and facility conditions
seoTitle: Folkston hunger strike at ICE facility

tea.why: Detained immigrants are protesting prolonged detention and alleged substandard conditions at the Folkston D Ray James ICE processing center.
tea.want: They demand release while their asylum and immigration cases proceed, protection from re-detention/deportation, and family reunification.
tea.changed: Oct 7: Advocates estimate at least 73 detained immigrants are participating in the hunger strike at the Folkston facility.

summary: A hunger strike began on October 6 at the Folkston D Ray James ICE processing center in south-east Georgia, involving at least 73 detained immigrants, according to advocates and family members. The protest targets prolonged detention, with some individuals held for 16 months to nearly three years without criminal charges. Detainees, many of whom are asylum seekers from various countries, also allege substandard conditions, including poor medical care, moldy food, and hostile guards. An open letter signed by 45 men was published, demanding their release while their immigration cases proceed, protection from re-detention, and family reunification. The facility is privately run by GEO Group.
organizers: Campaign to Shut Down the Folkston ICE processing center
demands: Release while pursuing asylum and immigration cases
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: at least 73 people, according to advocates and family members

updates.text: Detained immigrants began a hunger strike at the Folkston D Ray James ICE processing center.
Advocates estimate at least 73 detained immigrants are participating in the hunger strike.
An open letter signed by 45 detained immigrants was published, outlining their demands.
A lead organizer, Idris Makhmudov, was reportedly placed in solitary confinement this week.
Two Russian asylum seekers released a document detailing alleged facility violations.
